name: Barbara Jones
chief_complaint: Low mood and tiredness for 3 months
opening_statement: I've been feeling really down lately, Doctor. I just don't have the energy to do anything anymore, and I'm struggling to get through the day at work.
emotional_baseline: Flat affect, maintains minimal eye contact, speaks in monotone with occasional long pauses. Tearful when discussing impact on children. Cooperative but appears fatigued.

symptoms.duration: Present most days, worse in mornings
symptoms.characteristics: Describes feeling 'empty' and 'worthless', no longer enjoys activities with children
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Work stress, financial worries, lack of sleep
symptoms.relieving_factors: Brief improvement when distracted by children's activities
symptoms.associated_symptoms: Anhedonia, poor concentration, guilt about being 'a bad mother'

rag_citations.reference: Depression in adults - diagnostic criteria require depressed mood or anhedonia plus ≥4 additional symptoms for ≥2 weeks
rag_citations.relevance: Core diagnostic criterion for major depressive disorder

symptoms.characteristics: Feels exhausted even after full night's sleep, struggles to complete work tasks
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Physical exertion, afternoon worse than morning

rag_citations.reference: Fatigue is common somatic symptom in depression, present in 73% of cases with moderate severity

symptoms.characteristics: Early morning wakening at 3-4am, unable to return to sleep, ruminates about work failures
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Stress about finances, guilt about parenting

rag_citations.reference: Early morning wakening is characteristic of melancholic depression subtype, suggests need for antidepressant therapy

symptoms.characteristics: Lost 4kg unintentionally, eats 1-2 small meals daily, 'food has no taste'
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Nausea in mornings, no interest in cooking
symptoms.associated_symptoms: Guilt about not preparing family meals

symptoms.characteristics: Unable to complete reports at work, forgets meetings, re-reads emails multiple times
Believes she is 'failing as a mother', 'burden to family', thinks children 'would be better off without me'
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Evenings when alone, after arguments with partner
symptoms.relieving_factors: Engagement with children provides temporary respite
symptoms.associated_symptoms: Passive death wishes ('wish I wouldn't wake up') but denies active suicidal ideation or plan

rag_citations.reference: Passive suicidal ideation requires risk assessment and may warrant specialist referral if persistent despite initial treatment
rag_citations.relevance: Critical for safety planning and treatment intensity decision

past_medical_history.current_status: Stable on thyroxine 100mcg daily, TSH checked 4 months ago (normal)
Resolved after 6 months of sertraline 50mg and CBT, ceased medication 2017
Occasional (1-2 per month), managed with sumatriptan as needed
Recurrent, last ferritin 18 mcg/L (6 months ago), non-compliant with supplements due to constipation

medications.name: Ferrous sulfate
medications.compliance: Poor - stopped 2 months ago due to constipation

allergies: No known drug allergies. Reports mild nausea with codeine (not true allergy).
family_history: Mother: depression (treated with antidepressants age 45-60), currently well. Father: type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Sister: anxiety disorder. No family history of bipolar disorder, psychosis, or completed suicide.

social_history.occupation: Administration officer (part-time, 4 days/week) - works from home 3 days. Recent performance concerns from manager.
social_history.living_situation: Lives with partner (married 10 years) and 2 children (ages 9 and 7) in outer suburban Melbourne
social_history.support_system: Partner works full-time in trades (long hours), limited help with childcare. Mother lives interstate, sister nearby but busy. Feels isolated.

substance_use.alcohol: Previously social (1-2 drinks per week). Now 4-6 standard drinks on 2-3 evenings weekly (wine to help sleep) - recent increase concerns her.

social_history.exercise: Previously walked 30min x3/week, now struggles to exercise due to fatigue
social_history.stressors: Financial strain (partner's work irregular), eldest child having behavioral issues at school, relationship tension with partner ('he doesn't understand')

examination_findings.general: Appears stated age, casually dressed, adequate hygiene. Flat affect, psychomotor retardation noted.

mental_state_examination.speech: Reduced rate and volume, increased latency
mental_state_examination.thought: No flight of ideas, loosening of associations, or thought disorder. Denies hallucinations. Expresses passive suicidal ideation but denies intent or plan.
mental_state_examination.cognition: Alert, oriented x3. Subjective memory complaints. No formal cognitive testing done.
mental_state_examination.insight: Good - recognizes needs help, attributes symptoms to 'stress and exhaustion'

examination_findings.neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, normal tone and power, reflexes 2+ symmetric

required.rationale: Quantify depression severity, establish baseline for treatment monitoring
Exclude hypothyroidism exacerbation as cause of mood/fatigue symptoms
required.expected_result: TSH 2.1 mIU/L (normal), free T4 14 pmol/L (normal) - hypothyroidism well controlled

required.rationale: Assess for anaemia contributing to fatigue
required.expected_result: Hb 108 g/L (mild anaemia), MCV 76 fL (microcytic), consistent with iron deficiency

required.rationale: Confirm iron deficiency, guide replacement therapy

optional.rationale: Exclude B12/folate deficiency as contributor to mood symptoms
Screen for diabetes given family history and symptoms

interventions: Risk assessment: No active suicidal ideation/plan, but passive death wishes require safety planning
PHQ-9 score 16-18 confirms moderate-severe depression requiring pharmacotherapy + psychotherapy
Commence SSRI (sertraline 50mg daily - previously effective for postnatal depression, or escitalopram 10mg daily as alternative)
Educate: 2-4 weeks for symptom improvement, continue 6-12 months minimum even when feeling better
Safety plan: Crisis contacts (Lifeline 13 11 14, Beyond Blue 1300 22 4636), remove means if SI escalates
Address iron deficiency: Prescribe iron polymaltose 100mg daily (better tolerated) or IV iron if severe symptoms
Alcohol reduction advice: Discuss interaction with antidepressants, worsens depression, sets target <2 standard drinks/day
Review in 1-2 weeks: Monitor side effects (nausea, headache, sexual dysfunction), adherence, suicidal ideation
Repeat PHQ-9 at 2, 4, 8 weeks to track response (target >50% reduction by 8 weeks)
Refer psychology for CBT (MBS items 2721-2727, up to 10 sessions with GP Mental Health Treatment Plan)
GPMP + TCA (items 721 + 723): Coordinate care, involve partner in psychoeducation if patient consents
Increase SSRI dose if <50% improvement at 4 weeks (sertraline to 100mg or escitalopram to 20mg)
Repeat TFTs in 3 months if thyroxine dose stable
Recheck Hb and ferritin in 8-12 weeks after iron replacement commenced
Psychiatry: Active suicidal ideation with plan, psychotic features, treatment-resistant (failed 2 adequate trials)
Consider referral if no response to 2 antidepressants at therapeutic doses for 6-8 weeks each
Sleep hygiene: Regular sleep schedule, avoid screens 1h before bed, limit caffeine after 2pm
Physical activity: Start with 10min walks daily, gradual increase to 30min x5/week (evidence for mild-moderate depression)
Social connection: Encourage regular contact with sister, consider mother support groups, couples counseling if relationship strain persists
Work modifications: Discuss flexible hours or temporary reduced duties with employer via GP letter if needed

critical_errors.error: Fails to assess suicidal ideation, intent, and plan
critical_errors.consequence: Missed immediate safety risk - patient has passive death wishes requiring documentation and safety planning

critical_errors.error: Prescribes antidepressant without educating about 2-4 week onset delay
critical_errors.consequence: Patient may discontinue prematurely due to lack of immediate effect, leading to treatment failure

critical_errors.error: Does not check thyroid function despite hypothyroidism history
critical_errors.consequence: Misses potential thyroid dysfunction mimicking or exacerbating depression

critical_errors.error: Fails to address increasing alcohol use (4-6 drinks on 2-3 evenings)
critical_errors.consequence: Alcohol worsens depression, interacts with SSRIs, risk of developing dependence

critical_errors.error: Does not arrange psychology referral with Mental Health Treatment Plan
critical_errors.consequence: Delayed access to evidence-based psychotherapy (CBT), patient misses MBS-funded sessions

critical_errors.error: Ignores iron deficiency anaemia contributing to fatigue
critical_errors.consequence: Persistent fatigue despite antidepressant, reduced treatment response

fracp_reviews.comments: Clinically appropriate medium-difficulty case for AMC Clinical Exam. Depression severity, comorbidities (hypothyroidism, iron deficiency, hazardous alcohol use), and psychosocial stressors create realistic complexity. PHQ-9 score 16-18 justifies moderate-severe classification. Critical errors appropriately weighted - suicide risk assessment is non-negotiable. Management plan aligns with eTG and RANZCP guidelines. One suggestion: consider adding relationship/couples counseling as optional management given partner tension.

Strong case for GP-level depression management assessment. Passive suicidal ideation without intent/plan is common presentation requiring nuanced risk assessment - excellent teaching point. Sertraline choice justified by prior response (postnatal depression 2015). Appropriately flags specialist referral criteria (treatment resistance, active SI). Alcohol increase is realistic complication often missed by candidates. Learning objectives cover core competencies: suicide risk, PHQ-9 use, antidepressant initiation, psychotherapy access (MBS items). Approve for database inclusion.

learning_objectives: Apply PHQ-9 screening tool to quantify depression severity and establish treatment monitoring baseline (score ≥15 indicates moderate-severe, requires pharmacotherapy + psychotherapy)
Perform systematic suicide risk assessment: Differentiate passive ideation ('wish I wouldn't wake up') from active ideation with intent/plan, document protective factors (children, lack of means)
Select appropriate first-line antidepressant for moderate-severe depression: SSRI (sertraline 50mg or escitalopram 10mg) with consideration of prior response history and side effect profile
Utilize MBS-funded mental health services: GP Mental Health Treatment Plan (items 2721-2727) enables up to 10 psychology sessions, improves access to CBT
Recognize and manage comorbid conditions exacerbating depression: Check TSH (hypothyroidism), iron studies (anaemia causing fatigue), screen for hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C)
Educate patients on antidepressant expectations: 2-4 week onset delay, continue 6-12 months minimum post-remission, common side effects (nausea, sexual dysfunction, initial anxiety)
Implement evidence-based non-pharmacological interventions: CBT (first-line for mild-moderate depression), exercise prescription (30min x5/week equivalent to antidepressant effect), sleep hygiene
Identify specialist psychiatry referral indications: Active suicidal ideation with plan, psychotic features, treatment-resistant depression (failed ≥2 adequate antidepressant trials)
